items.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: I listened to two records that just kill me. A little known album by Karl Berger, done in the early nineties. It’s a semi-big-band with Enrico Rava and all sorts of people and with Ingrid Sertso singing called “No Man is an Island.”

ctx.x: Well that was a question I should have prepared you for. What do you listen to these days as far as jazz?

You know I listen to Pandora. I don’t go too much out of my way to sit down and listen, though I have it on. Sometimes Pandora and I have it tuned to Clifford Brown and also to bebop, stuff comes up. I just got another car with a great stereo system and I listened to two records that just kill me. A little known album by Karl Berger, done in the early nineties. It’s a semi-big-band with Enrico Rava and all sorts of people and with Ingrid Sertso singing called “No Man is an Island.” I could listen to that forever.…
